title: Introspective Calibration Breakdown: Where 'Do You Know This?' Stops Predicting Accuracy

original_idea.body: Introspective Calibration Breakdown. Problem: the boundary where introspective self-report honesty breaks down is under-mapped. Direction: ask a small open model to answer factual questions and predict in advance whether it will get each right, plot predicted-vs-actual calibration, stratify by complexity/length to locate where self-reports diverge from reality.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (locate where self-report calibration breaks -> deployer trust) but catastrophic-risk link is a gap.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Self-report confidence + calibration curve on public QA.

novelty.reasoning: Self-report calibration and its drop on complex prompts is documented; largely confirmatory.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Self-prediction calibration breakdown is already documented; this is a stratified replication.
